results.title: AI Cloud Compute Prices Rise Again As GPU Demand Stays Tight
results.author: Tech Help Canada Staff
highlights:
On Sept. 17, Investing.com reported, citing Bloomberg News and an emailed company statement, that Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1. The reported change applies to Nvidia H100, H200, B200, and B300 resources, along with certain CPU and memory resources.

Nebius’s public pricing page, viewed before the reported October change takes effect, listed on-demand rates of $3.85 per GPU-hour for HGX H100, $4.50 for HGX H200, $7.15 for HGX B200, and $7.85 for HGX B300.

...

## October is the next pricing checkpoint

Two timing details now stand out. The reported Nebius increases are set to begin Oct. 1, while AWS says current EC2 Capacity Block prices are scheduled to be updated in October 2026.

That makes October a key month for cloud AI buyers watching GPU capacity costs. If rates keep climbing, AI teams may face a tougher tradeoff between speed, certainty, and budget control. If capacity eases or more efficient infrastructure changes the equation, some pricing pressure may soften. For now, the signal from public GPU cloud pricing is clear: guaranteed AI compute remains expensive, and demand is still strong enough for providers to test higher rates.

results.title: Nebius Raised the Rent 21%.
results.author: ThePortablePortfolio
highlights:
### Nebius told customers its B300 rate goes from $7.85 to $9.50 an hour on Oct 1, the second increase since May. Suppliers sitting on a glut do not send that notice.

ThePortablePortfolio

Sep 23, 2026

The B300 goes from $7.85 an hour to $9.50 on October 1. The H100 goes from $3.85 to $4.50. H200, $4.50 to $5.40. B200, $7.15 to $8.50. Between 17% and 21%, depending on the chip, and it is the second increase Nebius has sent its customers since May.

...

There is a detail in this one that I keep coming back to. The new rates went out as a note to customers. The public pricing page still showed the old numbers. You raise prices quietly when you are confident the customers you already have will pay and you would rather not hand the number to a rival or a reporter.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU-hour rates a second time. The memory line is where the story is · FLUX | EchoVerse Dispatches
results.author: FLUX
highlights:
Nebius Group, the Amsterdam-based, Nasdaq-listed specialist GPU cloud, told customers in mid-September that on-demand prices for Nvidia GPU instances, AMD EPYC Genoa CPU capacity and Genoa memory will rise on 1 October.

...

Nebius Group (Nasdaq: NBIS), an Amsterdam-based neocloud (a specialist cloud provider that leases Nvidia GPU compute to AI labs and enterprises), notified customers in September 2026 that on-demand, pay-as-you-go prices will rise October 1, with GPU-hour rates climbing 17–21% and the per-GiB-hour rate for Genoa memory on AMD EPYC CPU-only compute rising about 41%. It is the company's second price increase in roughly four months, and the size of the memory increase matters because enterprise budgets rarely hedge that cost the way they hedge GPU hours.

...

Nebius Group, the Amsterdam-based, Nasdaq-listed specialist GPU cloud, told customers in mid-September that on-demand On-demand (pay-as-you-go) Cloud capacity billed by the hour with no term commitment, at the provider's published rate. prices for Nvidia GPU instances, AMD EPYC Genoa CPU capacity and Genoa memory will rise on 1 October. It is the second increase this year. The headline is a GPU-hour hike of roughly 17 to 21 percent depending on chip generation. The more interesting line, four rows down the notice, is memory.

The details come from a customer notice reported by Shattered.io, with Reuters framing (via Yahoo Finance) attributing the move to demand outrunning supply. Nebius had not formally confirmed the changes publicly as of reporting. ⁠ 1 1 David Prior, "Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) Stock Price Hike Signals Surging Demand For AI Compute Capacity," Foreign Policy Journal, 19 September 2026. https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/2026/09/19/nebius-nasdaq-nbis-stock-price-hike-signals-surging-demand-for-ai-compute-capacity Treat every figure below as reported from that notice, not company-confirmed.

## What the notice says

Per the customer communication as reported, on-demand pay-as-you-go GPU rates move as follows: H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 per hour (a rise of $0.65, or roughly 17%); H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (about 20%); B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (about 19%); B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 (about 21%). ⁠ 2 2 Dr. Heinrich Vogel, "Nebius Hikes AI Cloud Prices 21%, Memory Jumps 41% [2026]," Shattered.io, 23 September 2026. https://shattered.io/nebius-ai-cloud-price-hike-memory-2026 The oldest and most-deployed tier moves least; the newest Blackwell tier moves most.

Foreign Policy Journal and Barchart, citing the same notice, report AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU-hours rising 25% to $0.015 from $0.012, and memory pricing tied to those Genoa systems rising roughly 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. ⁠ 1 ⁠ 3 3 Aditya Raghunath, "Nebius Stock Spikes 4% on Higher Computer Prices," Barchart, 22 September 2026. https://www.barchart.com/story/news/4740983/nebius-stock-spikes-4-on-higher-computer-prices-how-to-play-nbis-stock-here The CPU and memory figures have not been independently corroborated by a primary source; they should be read as secondary reports.

The prior move sets the baseline. According to Shattered.io's account, Nebius already raised on-demand capacity by an average of 29% and spot capacity by 51% around May. ⁠ 2 Read the September notice against that: a customer who came on to on-demand pricing after May faces two increases inside a single planning cycle, while one who was already on on-demand pricing in May may face only the October increase; one report said the May rise did not apply to existing customers.

results.title: Everyone in the AI build is selling the same option to a different buyer
results.author: Haircut
highlights:
Nebius, which raised its price while the market fell.

On 17 September, Nebius told customers that selected pay-as-you-go GPU rates rise 17% to 21% on 1 October. H100 goes from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. By the 19th, the executed market went the other way. H100 was $2.85 versus $3.02 the day before and H200 was $5.13 versus $5.60. The new H100 card is 57.9% above the latest executed price.

I do not think that makes the list price useless though. Nebius still publishes preemptible rates of $2.15 for H100 and $2.45 for H200, and says a large multi-month reservation can get up to 35% off. Same accelerator, three prices. The fully flexible one is the one getting more expensive. You pay more if you want to turn up whenever you like.

Sources: Nebius pricing page and customer notice via Reuters, Ornn cross-GPU settlements. B300 is excluded because there is no executed settlement for it.

So the real product is the spread, not the price.

If the preemptible rates stay where they are, the on-demand premium on H100 goes from $1.70 to $2.35 an hour. B300 goes from $3.55 to $5.20. Nebius has not published future preemptible rates, so I am holding those flat for now. The price increase lands on the customer who refuses to commit.

Sources: Nebius pricing page and the announced 1 October on-demand reset. The second series assumes preemptible rates hold.

results.title: Your GPU provider can re-price your workloads with two weeks' notice. Nebius just did — again. | Peter Lee
results.author: Peter Lee
highlights:
On September 17, Nebius told customers that pay-as-you-go GPU rates rise October 1: H100s from $3.85 to $4.50/hr (+17%), B300s to $9.50 (+21%), CPU +25%, and memory-backed instances +41%. It's their second hike in three months.

Two things worth noting:
First, the steepest increase isn't on GPUs — it's memory (+41%). The binding constraint on AI compute right now isn't silicon, it's memory and the megawatts to run it. That's why even four-year-old H100s are getting more expensive to rent, not cheaper.

Second, the market loved it. NBIS jumped ~9% on the news. Investors read it as pricing power — capacity rationing, not distress. When your customers have nowhere else to go, you can move the rate card twice a quarter.
This is the FinOps lesson I keep coming back to: in GPU land, price predictability is becoming a genuine differentiator. The cheapest $/GPU-hr means nothing if the number changes before your budget cycle ends.

results.title: Nebius says it will raise AI cloud rental prices from… | Pivot News
results.author: James Okafor
highlights:
The Amsterdam-based neocloud firm's second increase in three months lifts pay-as-you-go rates for selected Nvidia GPUs by 17% to 21%, with memory offerings rising about 41%, though customers reserving large clusters for months can still get commitment discounts.

James Okafor September 19, 2026

Cloud provider Nebius will raise pay-as-you-go prices for leasing selected Nvidia chips starting October 1, the company said on Thursday, September 17, in comments reported by Reuters and carried by Economic Times Tech. It is the company's second price increase in three months. [1]

Rates for selected Nvidia graphics processing units will rise between 17% and 21%, according to the report. On-demand rates for some central processing units made by AMD and Intel, along with memory offerings, are also going up: the company said prices of some CPU-only instances will rise by 25% and memory offerings by about 41%. Customers reserving large-scale clusters for multiple months can receive commitment discounts. [1]

results.title: Nebius Raises Token Factory GPU Inference Prices Up to 20% Starting Oct. 1 | Gate News
results.author: GateNews
highlights:
1

2026-09-23 06:08:42

According to posts on X on Tuesday, Nebius is raising prices for its Token Factory managed inference platform by an average of 18.3%, effective Oct. 1. The increases target Pay-As-You-Go dedicated GPU endpoints, with high-end Nvidia configurations climbing sharply: H100 pricing rising 16% to $4.70 per hour, H200 up 19% to $5.60, B200 up 18% to $8.70, and B300 up 20% to $9.70 per hour. Existing contractual pricing and active reservations remain unchanged. Nebius attributed the hikes to sustained demand for GPU capacity. The move follows earlier price increases for on-demand cloud GPU rental rates. Last month, Nebius reported Q2 AI Cloud revenue surged 514% to $574.9 million, with adjusted EBITDA reaching $236.2 million.
